definitions.explanation: The daughter of a prince, duke, or other high-ranking nobleman. Used primarily in European historical and literary contexts when translated into Japanese.

examples.japanese: {公女|こうじょ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{城|しろ}→城：03255_shiro⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{育|そだ}った→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧。
examples.english: The princess grew up in a castle.

examples.japanese: ⟦{物語|ものがたり}→物語：03634_monogatari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{公女|こうじょ}だった。
examples.english: The protagonist of the story was a princess of a certain country.

examples.japanese: {歴史小説|れきししょうせつ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{公女|こうじょ}たち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{政略結婚|せいりゃくけっこん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{描|えが}かれる→描く：02013_egaku⟧。
examples.english: In historical novels, political marriages of princesses are often depicted.

notes:
Composed of {公|こう} (duke, public, noble) and {女|じょ} (woman, daughter). Primarily used as a translation equivalent for European titles like "princess" or "duke's daughter" in historical and literary contexts. Not used for Japanese imperial princesses, who are called ⟦{皇女|こうじょ}→皇女：24369_koujo⟧ (same pronunciation, different first kanji).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{皇女|こうじょ}→皇女：24369_koujo⟧ — imperial princess (daughter of an emperor; same reading, different kanji)
- ⟦{王女|おうじょ}→王女：04108_oujo⟧ — princess (daughter of a king)
- ⟦{姫|ひめ}→姫：12233_hime⟧ — princess, young lady (broader, more common in daily speech and stories)
- ⟦{令嬢|れいじょう}→令嬢：11609_reijou⟧ — young lady of good family (not specifically noble)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {公女|こうじょ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{身分|みぶん}→身分：00278_mibun⟧ — the status of a princess
- {公女|こうじょ}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{育|そだ}つ→育つ：01951_sodatsu⟧ — to be raised as a princess
